subject.title: I updated Scrapling and the skill became hidden again

question: Should Scrapling continue receiving full per-version quarantine, or should maintainers approve a narrowly scoped durable trust treatment after reviewing its recurring private scanner evidence?
rationale: The source tree cannot determine whether the repeated verdict is a scanner defect, an expected finding in each changed artifact, or a case appropriate for a trusted-publisher exception; that choice changes a security boundary.

options.title: Investigate and preserve the gate
options.body: Review the latest private scan evidence, correct any reproducible false-positive rule, and keep per-version quarantine unless the new artifact actually clears.

options.title: Approve a narrow trust exception
options.body: Grant Scrapling a documented and audited exception that bypasses only the recurring pending-scan behavior while retaining malicious and high-impact blocking.

options.title: Keep manual review
options.body: Continue requiring a moderator to review each new version, accepting the recurring publisher-support burden as the security policy.

recommendation.title: Investigate and preserve the gate
recommendation.body: Review the latest private scan evidence, correct any reproducible false-positive rule, and keep per-version quarantine unless the new artifact actually clears.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the active content-policy discussion governing public visibility and human-review treatment, while implementation details can be routed to the moderation contributors.
